s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute painful skin lesion with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful, warm, and nodular skin lesion
History of similar lesion that resolved spontaneously
Presence of Gram-negative coccobacilli on Gram stain
key_facts: 34-year-old breastfeeding woman
Subacute painful skin lesion between neck and breast
Lesion measures approximately 3 × 4 cm
Patient visited East-Turkish region one year earlier
Similar lesion occurred one year earlier and resolved after 10 days
Patient has history of premature birth and intracerebral bleeding
Patient has VP shunt due to hydrocephaly
Leukocyte count is elevated at 11.15 × 10⁹/L
C-reactive protein is elevated at 15 mg/L
Ultrasound shows inflammatory subcutaneous collection
Aspirate microscopy shows amorphous debris and neutrophil granulocytes
Gram staining shows Gram-negative coccobacilli

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram-negative coccobacilli and positive culture for B. melitensis biovar 3

shortlist.label: Cellulitis due to Gram-negative bacteria
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and Gram-negative coccobacilli

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute painful skin lesion and history of similar lesion

shortlist.label: Nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute painful skin lesion and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium fortuitum infection
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute painful skin lesion and history of immunocompromised state

raw.rationale: The patient's history of visiting an East-Turkish region, where Brucellosis is endemic, and the presence of Gram-negative coccobacilli in the Gram stain, which is consistent with Brucella species, support this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient's symptoms of a subacute painful skin lesion and elevated inflammatory markers are also consistent with Brucellosis.

rejected.label: Cellulitis due to Gram-negative bacteria
rejected.why: While the Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli, the patient's symptoms and history are more specific for Brucellosis

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: Actinomycosis typically presents with a more chronic and suppurative infection, which is not consistent with the patient's subacute presentation

rejected.label: Nocardiosis
rejected.why: Nocardiosis typically affects immunocompromised patients and presents with a more severe and disseminated infection, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Mycobacterium fortuitum infection
rejected.why: Mycobacterium fortuitum infection typically presents with a more chronic and localized infection, and the patient's symptoms and history are more consistent with Brucellosis

gold: Brucella melitensis soft tissue abscess related to ventriculoperitoneal shunt
